verdict.rationale: Supermemory documents genuine self-hosting: 'runs on your own hardware... as a single self-contained binary' with local graph engine, embeddings, and LLM so 'data never leaves the building.' However, the docs explicitly state 'No Docker. No database to provision. No config files' — the opposite of the story's Docker-based open-source deployment model — and there is no evidence the self-hosted binary is distributed as open-source code (vs. a proprietary binary), so the specific packaging/openness expectations are not met. Missing for 10: confirmed open-source repo/license for the self-hosted engine, official Docker image/Compose file, and independent verification of a successful self-hosted deployment.
